note.label: Psalm 37: Fret Not Because of Evildoers

precepts.why:
“But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the Lord shall be as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; into smoke shall they consume away.” Zephaniah names who is on that list: “it shall come to pass in the day of the Lord’s sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, and the king’s children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel.” Strange apparel goes against what the Bible says, like women in pants.

That day is the evil time, and “A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked”, for neither their silver nor their gold is going to save them in it. The righteous “shall not be ashamed in the evil time: and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.” That is why we have food pantries in our cities: when the days of famine come, the Most High will make sure we are satisfied. All you have to do is get in touch with your leadership in your state, and there is no shame in it.

precepts.text: Neither their silver nor their gold shall deliver them in the day of the Most High's wrath, for the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy.
precepts.point: Riches are uncertain; money in an online bank cannot be reached when Wi-Fi and electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
Zephaniah says the same of the day of the Lord: “Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord’s wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy”. He will “make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.” Those who boast in the multitude of their riches will find their silver and gold cannot ransom them when the wrath comes.

Riches profit not in the day of wrath, and they cannot redeem a brother from the grave. Trust in uncertain riches fails at both ends; the living God is the only sure trust.

precepts.why: The way you dress stipulates what you believe: you know a Roman Catholic priest, a Buddhist, a Muslim by their clothes. “I will punish the princes, and the king’s children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel.” God says he will destroy those in strange apparel. He gave us a dress code: fringes, and a border of blue upon all your garments.

points: The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly. It is coming, brothers; you can see the things that are happening; time is speeding up.
The mighty man shall cry there bitterly: these dudes that think they are tough are going to cry bitterly.

That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness: there will be thick darkness all over America and all over the world.

A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities and against the high towers: the fenced cities are the protected cities. You are going to hear the alarm, the warning going all over the television, that the missiles are coming, within one hour.
I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the Lord: and their blood shall be poured out as dust, and their flesh as the dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord's wrath. No matter how much money you get, it cannot deliver you in the day of God's wrath. Those of you that are rich in this world: do not save your riches up in this world; help with the work.
But the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.
The word of the Lord which came unto Zephaniah in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.
